newsitem.title: USA: AlliedSignal turns to UPS for distribution.
newsitem.headline: AlliedSignal turns to UPS for distribution.

text.p: AlliedSignal Automotive Aftermarket said Wednesday it has contracted UPS Worldwide Logistics to distribute products from AlliedSignal's North American manufacturing plants to 10,000 customer locations across North America.

Under the multi-year $300 million-plus agreement, UPS Worldwide Logistics will design, establish and maintain two regional U.S. distribution centers and a best-in-class logistics network as part of the company's supply chain re- engineering initiative, the AlliedSignal Inc subsidiary said.
UPS Worldwide Logistics is a subsidiary of United Parcel Service of America Inc.

Over the next 12-20 months, UPS Worldwide Logistics will consolidate AlliedSignal Automotive Aftermarket's five distribution facilities into two highly automated regional distribution centers -- in Reno, Nev., and Hebron, Ky., the company said.

UPS Worldwide Logistics will begin moving inventory and migrating information systems to these locations within the 1998 timeframe. The existing AlliedSignal Automotive Aftermarket distribution facilities are scheduled to phase out by the end of 1998, the company said.
AlliedSignal spokesman Russell Dubner said those facilities are in Santa Fe Springs, Calif.; Clearfield, Utah; Greenville, Ohio; and Jackson and Bemis, Tenn.
He was unable to say how many layoffs would result from the closings or what the company meant by a multi-year agreement. ((-- New York Newsdesk 212-859-1610.))
